summary.headline: IFGL consolidated PAT rose 102% YoY to ~Rs 26 crore in Q2 FY27 on total income of ~Rs 555 crore, while standalone EBITDA margin slipped to 10.8%.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income grew about 13% YoY to ~Rs 555 crore in Q2 FY27 and consolidated EBITDA rose about 28% to ~Rs 61 crore (9.2% margin). Standalone gross margin fell to 43.9% from 45.2% on higher raw material and input costs, and standalone EBITDA was ~Rs 35 crore versus Rs 37 crore a year earlier. Export sales grew about 40% YoY while domestic sales grew 5%. The company terminated its JV with Marvel International Group effective October 14, 2026, and Rs 1.69 crore of the JV investment was impaired. Operating cash flow improved by ~Rs 68 crore in H1 FY27 versus ~Rs 8 crore a year earlier.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 37 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Standalone India domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic sales grew 5% YoY in Q2 FY27, described by management as steady with strong momentum. Management guided to roughly 60-70% India capacity utilisation.

segments.name: Standalone exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue grew about 40% YoY in Q2 FY27. Management said growth is concentrated in the Middle East, Turkey and Asia, with Europe subdued.

segments.name: Europe (UK, Germany, Hoffman, Sheffield)
segments.commentary: European segment returned to positive segment result in Q2 FY27 versus a loss a year earlier. Hoffman Ceramic in the Czech Republic completed voluntary liquidation effective July 1, 2026.

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: Management described strong revenue growth and a significant improvement in segment profitability. US steel production was up 6% YoY at 75 million tonnes YTD October 2026.

segments.name: China (Monocon subsidiary)
segments.commentary: New Talc/clay plant with 2,000 tpa capacity commenced commercial operations, with potential annual revenue of ~Rs 20-25 crore at full utilisation. Management did not disclose Monocon's H1 revenue growth or margins.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 9-10% for FY27.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at double digits, with management saying it is working to push it higher.
Standalone FY27 capex of about Rs 40-50 crore; next-year capex not yet finalised, to be discussed around March.
Debottlenecking underway for a couple of product lines; incremental capacity expected from next year, not this year.
Management expects Q3 FY27 in Europe to be as encouraging as expected, with the Christmas holiday impact offset by sales across the group's plants.
Middle East growth potential remains, but management declined to quantify it given geopolitical uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capital work in progress closing balance was about Rs 39 crore, spread across India, Khurda and a US project; management did not give a March 2027 figure but said there would be no major increase.
China Monocon Talc/clay plant: 2,000 tpa installed capacity, pitch-free and tar-free clay for blast furnace use, built with technical support from Sheffield Refractories UK.

India: phase one of the technology transfer for a product line is complete and the company is in phase two. Equipment is partly due in December 2026 and an imported pump by mid-February or March 2027.
Khurda project: no finalised course of action yet because of political issues; management said new timelines will follow.
Marvel JV land asset retained; management said it will be used in due course and that alternative options for the JV opportunity are being evaluated.
demand_pricing: Management expects Indian steel demand to rise with production, with the company pushing sales growth in India and selected US areas.
Export growth is focused on the Middle East, Turkey and Asia. European demand is subdued.

Pricing: most Indian contracts are refractory management and service contracts, renegotiated periodically. Cost pressure is passed on through customer-by-customer price increases, and management says customers are supporting increases.
Raw material costs (alumina, magnesia) have not trended down and are rising because of the ongoing war. Management said pass-through to customers was achieved with a time lag.
Management declined to split revenue by product, including the non-steel share and new product contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Will Indian steel capacity additions drive exponential demand for the company's products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is rising with steel production and it is raising sales in India and some US areas. Exports are growing with Middle East and Turkey focus. No product-wise revenue split was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 39 crore consolidated CWIP and how is refractory pricing set?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP is a mix of India, Khurda and US projects, with no major increase expected. Pricing is mostly negotiated periodically under management contracts and passed through as customer-specific price increases, with customers aware of global market moves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Marvel JV termination, and is Europe's Q3 affected by Christmas holidays?
qa_highlights.answer: Marvel JV has ended but management is evaluating alternatives. Management said the Europe Christmas impact should balance out because plants in Germany and the UK serve sales outside Europe, so Q3 should be encouraging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Monocon China plant's investment and product profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the investment as about Rs 2 crore against Rs 20-25 crore annual revenue at full utilisation, with a long gestation and stabilisation phase. It is a geographical expansion using existing Sheffield technology.

qa_highlights.question: Is capacity sufficient and how much KPEX is planned for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is ample apart from debottlenecking in a couple of product lines, with output from next year. FY27 KPEX is about Rs 40-50 crore; FY28 spend to be discussed in March.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass on raw material cost increases, and how is employee cost trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material prices are not falling and are rising, but customers are supporting price increases, which keeps the impact limited. Employee cost as a percentage of sales is up about 50 bps and is expected to stay at this level through FY27.

risks_watch: Standalone gross margin compression (43.9% vs 45.2%) from raw material costs, with the pass-through lag still a risk.
Europe subdued demand and the Christmas-holiday quarter; Hoffman and Sheffield integration still in progress.
Marvel JV termination: alternative plans for the Gujarat cement/green product capacity and land asset are unclear.
Khurda project timelines are undefined because of political issues.
US supply-chain disruption, freight costs and longer lead times, which management says it is trying to mitigate.
Middle East demand is uncertain; management declined to quantify it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on consolidated profit recovery and export growth, but cautious on standalone margins and Europe. Management was evasive on product-wise revenue, Monocon's financials, Khurda timelines and Middle East numbers, citing uncertainty.
key_quotes: Operating cash flows have improved significantly compared with the previous year, supported by better management of receivables, improved inventory control and greater discipline in working capital utilization.

While standalone operating margins remain under pressure due to higher input costs and the prevailing pricing environment, we have continued to focus on appropriate pricing solutions, cost optimization and operational efficiencies.
The facility has an installed capacity of 2000 metric tons per annum and is designed to manufacture pitch free tar free Tappel Clay for blast furnace applications.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone gross margin fell to 43.9% from 45.2% and standalone EBITDA margin to 10.8%, with raw material costs still rising; consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9-10%, a cut, and management is only working to push standalone margin higher.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation is only 60-70% and management says capacity is ample; debottlenecking in a couple of product lines brings incremental capacity from next year, not this year, with the China talc plant (2,000 tpa) already commissioned and small (~Rs 20-25 crore annual revenue at full utilisation).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Export revenue grew about 40% YoY in Q2 FY27 and domestic sales grew 5%, with management pushing India and US sales as Indian steel output rises (US steel output up 6% YTD); Europe subdued and Middle East uncertain.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 60-70% with ample capacity; FY27 capex is Rs 40-50 crore and FY28 capex is to be discussed around March, with no major CWIP increase (CWIP about Rs 39 crore).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Consolidated FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9-10% (a cut, not a raise), standalone margins compressing (gross margin 43.9% vs 45.2%), and management declined to quantify Middle East demand.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw materials (alumina, magnesia) are rising due to the war and pass-through to customers lags; standalone EBITDA fell to Rs 35 crore from Rs 37 crore YoY, and Europe is subdued into the Christmas quarter.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Technology transfer for a product line is in phase two with equipment partly due December 2026 and an imported pump by mid-February or March 2027, but no product launch dates or revenue were given.

rows.label: Export growth in Middle East, Turkey and Asia
rows.why: Exports grew about 40% YoY in Q2 FY27 concentrated in Middle East, Turkey and Asia, though management declined to quantify Middle East potential given geopolitical uncertainty.

rows.label: Marvel JV terminated; land asset retained
rows.why: JV terminated effective Oct 14, 2026 with Rs 1.69 crore impaired; the land asset is retained and alternative options are being evaluated, with no plan or timing disclosed.

rows.label: Customer price increases to offset raw material inflation
rows.why: Alumina and magnesia costs are rising, and management says customers are supporting customer-by-customer price increases, though with a time lag that is compressing standalone gross margin (43.9% vs 45.2%).
